calls.why: His erectors were loaded hard 24 hours ago: 4 ascending sets of smith bent-over row topping at 150x9 on 2026-07-28. Tonight's RDL is the only other heavy hinge in the week and it already sits at a clean 205x8 double from 2026-07-22. Repeat 2026-07-22 exactly; do not add load on a back that worked yesterday. This is the one lift tonight where the cost of being wrong is a lumbar strain, not a missed rep.

No readiness signal either way. Reps held across the working sets on 2026-07-22 (140x12, 160x11, 160x12), quads were last loaded three days ago on 2026-07-26 and handled 220x10, and he wrote no complaint about either. Nothing here for the brake to grab; load is the program seat's call.
Hamstrings show no accumulated fatigue: 135x13 twice on 2026-07-26 beat the flat 135x10s from 2026-07-22, three days of separation, no note. I see nothing to brake.

Trending the right way with no distress: 142.5x14 twice then 150x11 on 2026-07-26, versus 142.5 for 11/14/14 on 2026-07-22. Rest between those sets stayed short (roughly 45-75s). No fatigue signal to act on.

Calves are the one muscle he trims himself. On 2026-07-22 he ran four sets including a self-selected 260x15 back-off, then on 2026-07-26 he stopped calves at two sets of 260x15. That is a voluntary volume cut three days ago on a muscle that gets hit on both leg days. Repeat 2026-07-22's weights, no increase, and treat the fourth set as optional rather than owed.

Trunk is loaded on every leg day and tonight also carries the RDL. He crunched 55 for 13/12/12 on 2026-07-26 plus three sets of hanging leg raises the same night. Repeat 2026-07-22 (50x15) rather than chasing the 55; the abs are not the limiting adaptation this week and fresh erectors matter more for the RDL.

The only silent regression in the whole window: 60s holds on 2026-07-15 became 45s holds on 2026-07-22, twice, with no note explaining it. He complains loudly when something is wrong, so a quiet 25% cut reads as an honest end-of-session limit, not laziness. Hold at 45s and let him earn it back; do not prescribe 60s.
